claim: The sound tables are priority-then-(code,length) rows: the format header states 'PIRORITY,SOUND,LENGTH', which is what licenses reading the first FCB operand of every table below as its arbitration priority (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8046).

source.verbatim: *	 PIRORITY,SOUND,LENGTH (IF M.S.BIT SET ON SOUND, SOUND,LENGTH)

claim: A sound CODE in the range 01-3E is what is sent to the sound board; the board's own firmware (what a code sounds like) is not in the vendored tree, so every jt5 sample is a recording or a synthesis, never a bake from source (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8049).
SNEDIE is the ENEMY DIES table at priority 040 — the jt5-1 cue 'enemyDeath' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8104); played at the enemy-death call site (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2960).

SNPDIE is the PLAYER DIES table at priority 080 — the jt5-1 cue 'playerDeath' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8115). It sends the same 6-bit code $16 as SNEDIE at double the priority, so the two are distinct sounds and not one sound reused.
SNEGG is the PLAYER HITS EGG SOUND table at priority 045 — the jt5-1 cue 'eggCollected' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8098); played from the EGGSCR collision path (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3031).

source.verbatim: SNEGG	FCB	045,!N$03!.$7F,30	PLAYER HITS EGG SOUND

claim: SNEGGH is the EGG HATCHING SOUND table at priority 045 — the jt5-1 cue 'eggHatched' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8099); played where a settled egg matures (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3243).
SNPTEI is the PTERODACTYL INTRODUCTION SCREAM table at priority 065 — the jt5-1 cue 'pteroArrives' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8094); played on the pterodactyl's introduction (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1467).
SNPTED is the PTERODACTYL DYING SOUND table at priority 066 — the jt5-1 cue 'pteroDeath' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8091); played on the ptero kill (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2946).

SNPCR1 is the PLAYER 1 RE-CREATED (TRANSPORTER) table at priority 070 — the jt5-1 cue 'playerMaterialise' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8116). It is bound to the knight through P1DEC's decision block rather than a direct load (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5544); P2 carries its own table SNPCR2 (:8119), which jt5-1 collapses onto this one.
SNECRE is the ENEMY RE-CREATED (TRANSPORTER) table at priority 040 — the jt5-1 cue 'enemyMaterialise' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8103); bound through the enemy decision block (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5560).
SNREPL is the EXTRA MAN table at priority 100 — the highest priority in the whole sound set, and the jt5-1 cue 'extraMan' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8089); played from the REPLAY award (JOUSTRV4.SRC:7406).
SNBOUN is the COLLECT BOUNTY table at priority 050 — the jt5-1 cue 'waveBounty' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8096); played on the bounty award (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4711).
SNCLIF is the CLIFF DESTROYER table at priority 067 — the jt5-1 cue 'cliffDestroyed' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8090); played where a cliff is destroyed (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2327).

The single-voice PRIORITY arbitration jt5-1's channel map is built around: SND refuses a lower-priority interruption, comparing the incoming priority against the sounding one and branching away (SYSTEM.SRC:767).

source.verbatim: CMPA	SPRI		OK TO INTERUPT THIS PIRORITY SOUND?

claim: The flap is a TWO-LOOP coroutine, not a per-frame edge test: FLIPLP's TSTB/BNE GOFLAP leaves the wings-up loop for GOFLAP only when the button reads pressed (JOUSTRV4.SRC:6195-6196); a held button re-enters at FLAPS2/FLIPS2, BELOW each JSR VSND, which is why holding never re-fires the cue.

SNPLWD is the PLAYERS WING DOWN SOUND table at priority 010 — the jt5-3 cue 'playerWingDown' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8126); the machine loads it at GOFLAP's tail, FLAST2 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:6217), a 1982 copy-paste comment that reads 'GET WING UP SOUND' over the DSNWD load — trust the symbol, not the comment.

source.verbatim: SNPLWD	FCB	010,!N$20!.$7F,90	PLAYERS WING DOWN SOUND

claim: SNPLWU is the PLAYERS WING UP SOUND table at priority 010 — the jt5-3 cue 'playerWingUp' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8125); the machine loads it at GOFLIP (JOUSTRV4.SRC:6183), on the button RELEASE.

source.verbatim: SNPLWU	FCB	010,!N$21!.$7F,90	PLAYERS WING UP SOUND

claim: SNELWD is the ENEMIES WING DOWN SOUND table at priority 006 — the jt5-3 cue 'enemyWingDown' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8108). The row states the priority; what that priority then DOES is a property of SND, claimed separately as JT55-001.

source.verbatim: SNELWD	FCB	006,!N$20!.$7F,60	ENEMIES WING DOWN SOUND

claim: SND refuses a strictly lower priority than the one already sounding — 'CMPA SPRI / BLO NOSND' at SYSTEM.SRC:767-768, inside the routine at SYSTEM.SRC:761-773. So SNELWD's 006 (JT53-004) being below the player wing pair's 010 means a buzzard's wingbeat never steals the knight's own. Two qualifiers the comparison itself carries: BLO is unsigned branch-if-LOWER, so an EQUAL priority DOES interrupt; and the comparison only runs while STMR is non-zero (SYSTEM.SRC:765-766), so once the sounding table's frame window has expired any priority is accepted with no comparison at all. jt5-5 implements this, so the sentence is now true of this port and not only of the machine.

source.verbatim: CMPA	SPRI		OK TO INTERUPT THIS PIRORITY SOUND?

claim: SNELWU is the ENEMIES WING UP SOUND table at priority 006 — the jt5-3 cue 'enemyWingUp' (JOUSTRV4.SRC:8107).

source.verbatim: SNELWU	FCB	006,!N$21!.$7F,60	ENEMIES WING UP SOUND

claim: The knight's decision block binds SNPLWU/SNPLWD (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5544) — the jt5-3 call site for both player wing cues, chosen over GOFLIP/GOFLAP because those two lines load through the DSNWU/DSNWD structure OFFSETS (declared JOUSTRV4.SRC:118-119) and never name the table by symbol.
The buzzard's decision block binds SNELWU/SNELWD (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5560) — the jt5-3 call site for both enemy wing cues, the same binding enemyMaterialise already cites for SNECRE on this row.

A flap TAKE-OFF sounds wing-down: STFLY ends with a jump straight onto FLAST2, the same wing-down cue GOFLAP reaches — so entering flight by pressing the button is NOT silent, unlike walking off a ledge (STFALL, which re-enters below both cues).

SNPTHD is the AT LEAST 1 PERSON THUD'ED table at priority 020 — the jt5-4 cue 'playerThud'; played from the PLAYERS COLIDE call site (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5014). It is NOT 'two players': the table's own comment says AT LEAST ONE, and OSTBO (the only door to it) is reached for buzzard-vs-player as well as player-vs-player.

source.verbatim: SNPTHD	FCB	020,!N$08!+$80,30,$00,1	AT LEAST 1 PERSON THUD'ED

claim: SNETHD is the ENEMIES THUD table at priority 009 — the jt5-4 cue 'enemyThud'; played from the ENEMIES COLIDE call site (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5019). It sends the same 6-bit code $08 as SNPTHD at a lower priority, so the two are distinct sounds and not one sound reused.

The SNETHD path bumps through a HEIGHT TEST: OSTH11 (reached when neither party can kill the other, i.e. both enemy) calls OSTBMP, which compares the two entities' screen Y and dispatches — the physically higher bird always rises. This is the mechanism jt5-4's 'enemy-thud' branch ports as 'the smaller pixel Y takes bounceTop'.

source.verbatim: OSTH11	JSR	OSTBMP		NO-ONE DIES, BUT BUMP EACH OTHER ANYWAYS

claim: OSTBMP's dispatch is a screen-Y compare, not a register-role pick: it loads one entity's PPOSY+1 byte, subtracts the other's, and branches PLUS (>=0, so a tie included) to OSTUTP — the fall-through takes OSTXTP. Both arms send the physically higher bird up (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5099 'JSR OSTXUP MOVE REG.U GUY UP' in the OSTUTP arm, :5108 'JSR OSTXUP & REG.X GUY UP' in the OSTXTP arm), so height alone decides which entity takes which role.

source.verbatim: OSTBMP	LDB	PPOSY+1,X	DETERMINATION OF WHO HAS BEEN BUMPED

claim: The SNPTHD path bumps with NO height test: the exact lance-height tie OSTBO finds (':5010 BEQ 1$ BR=BOTH ON SAME LEVEL') reaches OSTXTT via ':5017 BRA OSTXTT', which calls OSTXTP UNCONDITIONALLY and never enters OSTBMP. OSTXTT is NOT exclusive to that tie — the non-ptero KILL path (OSTXT3, the lance-height WINNER) also falls into it from :5048-5052; the ONLY branch in that range is ':5052 BEQ OSTXPT', which diverts a PTERODACTYL winner into ':5056 EXG X,U / :5057 JSR PTEBRD' — a different continuation — so a non-ptero winner is the case that falls through — but that second entry plays no part in this story, which wires only the `bounce` outcome. Which bird rises on the tie is therefore fixed by REGISTER ROLE, not by where either one is — the mechanism jt5-4's 'player-thud' branch ports as a fixed, geometry-independent role assignment (the outer loop's object always takes OSTXDN, the one it found always takes OSTXUP), and JOUSTRV4.SRC:4874-4884 (the collision scan driver, not the bouncer) is what makes that assignment a ROM fact rather than a port choice: 'LDU PLINK,U' walks the process list into U and 'LEAX ,U' / 'LDX PLINK,X' starts X at U and walks it forward, so U is always the earlier element of a pair and X always the later one.

source.verbatim: OSTXTT	JSR	OSTXTP		REG.X WILL BE RESTORIED

claim: P7DEC, the pterodactyl's decision block, binds the SAME wing-up/wing-down tables as every buzzard block (SNELWU, SNELWD in slots 1 and 2). The row is COMPLETE on its own line: its nine FDB words map one-for-one onto the nine sound offsets DSNWU through DSNCRE declared at JOUSTRV4.SRC:118-126, so no continuation line extends it. This binding is the QUESTION jt5-10 answers, not the answer: a decision block's sound field means nothing unless something loads through it.

A pterodactyl is created by PTERST (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1423) / BAITST (:1427), and creation ends by branching to PTESTF — a label INSIDE the body of the PTEFLY flight loop (:1491-1510). So the bird begins life in its own loop and never passes through the knight/buzzard ground-and-flight state machine that owns the wing cues.

PTEFLY is a CLOSED loop: its final instruction is an unconditional branch back to its own head, so control never falls out of the bottom into neighbouring code. Note what a PJOY swap does NOT do: storing a new intelligence address into PJOY (STD PJOY,U) changes which routine AIROVR calls on the NEXT wake, and does not touch the process PC — so the swap leaves control inside this loop rather than escaping it. This is the hop that makes the wing loaders unreachable.

Every reference to a flap-loop label (FLAPLP, FLIPLP, FLAPS2, FLIPS2, FLAPST, FLIPST, GOFLIP, GOFLAP, FLAST2, WINGDN, WINGFK) in the whole of JOUSTRV4.SRC lies within :6135-6226. Only three of those mentions sit outside the loop body itself, and this line is one: it is the tail of STFLY (label at :6123, under the header comment 'START TO FLY' at :6121). The other two are STFALL's BNE FLAPS2 / BRA FLIPS2 (:6156-6157). Both routines are GROUND-state transitions — taking off, and falling off a cliff — which a bird that never lands cannot make. SRCADP clamps the pterodactyl at $D3-1 and clears PVELY (:1526-1531), and PTEFLY never calls CKGND.

AIROVR ends by returning the joystick word in registers A and B, so a pterodactyl is handed the flap bit on every wake exactly as a buzzard is. The buzzard's loops act on that register with TSTB (:6168, :6195); PTEFLY contains no TSTB and no reference to DSNWU or DSNWD, so the value is discarded. Being given the bit and ignoring it is what distinguishes a bird with no wing cue from a bird that was never offered one.

source.verbatim: LDD	CURJOY		GIVE BACK JOYSTICK POSITION

claim: The sixth word of P7DEC's first row is 0 where the buzzard blocks carry PLYR3/PLYR4/PLYR5, which invites the reading that a pterodactyl has no animation table. The decision-block offset map refutes it: field 6 is DPLYR, the RIDER'S image. A pterodactyl carries no rider, so the zero is expected and says nothing about flapping. The bird's wing ANIMATION is real and lives elsewhere — PTESEQ (:1580-1583) cycles FLY1, FLY2, FLY3, FLY2 on an 8-tick hold driven by the frame timer in PTESTF (:1493-1503), with no flap bit involved.

OSTH12 is the ptero-pair dispatch inside the no-kill branch: with SNETHD already sounded (:5019-5020), OSTHT2's PID tests found the FIRST party to be a pterodactyl and branched here; OSTH12 then tests the SECOND party's PID for #$80+PTEID. Both parties pterodactyls is the QUESTION its own comment asks ('2 PTERODACTYL'S?').

Two pterodactyls take the ORDINARY enemy bump: OSTH12's compare answering YES branches to OSTH11 ('SAME OLD COLISION'), which is JSR OSTBMP — no-one dies, the pair bumps apart by the height dispatch, and SNETHD is already playing. This is the routing jt5-16 ports: a ptero/ptero pair emits enemy-thud and resolves through the same bounce as a buzzard/buzzard pair. The unmeasured arm is the OTHER branch — a ptero/bird pair goes to PTEBRD (:5034) — which stays unbuilt in this port until its own story measures it.

source.verbatim: BEQ	OSTH11		BR=YES, SAME OLD COLISION
